title: Can pressure support a particle?

study.title: Can pressure support a particle?
study.summary: Compare standing-wave radiation force with gravity, inside a declared small-particle approximation.

inputs.label: Acoustic frequency
inputs.meaning: Cycles of sound pressure per second.

inputs.label: Peak antinode pressure
inputs.meaning: Standing-wave peak pressure in pascals; must be calibrated independently, not inferred from supply voltage.

inputs.label: Particle radius
inputs.meaning: Spherical particle radius; Rayleigh validity depends on a times wave number.

inputs.label: Particle density
inputs.meaning: Assumed particle density; not a measured specimen.

inputs.label: Acoustic contrast
inputs.meaning: Assumed dimensionless material contrast. It is not fitted to force an equilibrium.

assumptions: One-dimensional standing wave in air: density 1.204 kg/m3, sound speed 343 m/s.
Small spherical particle, weak linear field, no streaming, heating, viscosity correction or stability guarantee.

The visible concept bead is 8 mm in diameter for illustration, outside this small-particle model at 40 kHz. The default calculation uses a 0.2 mm diameter particle. No force prediction is attached to the rendered bead.
setup: Use a manufacturer-rated acoustic levitator as a supervised apparatus lead; this scene is not a wiring or drive design.
Measure air conditions, particle size/density and peak pressure with a calibrated suitable microphone.
Record particle displacement with a scale and camera; compare predicted and observed positions while varying drive.
controls: Change radius, material contrast and pressure independently.
study.falsifier: A pressure/radius sweep inconsistent with the declared force law after calibration rejects this ideal approximation for that apparatus.
study.scope: Simulated force support, not antigravity. Momentum is exchanged with the acoustic apparatus.

metrics.label: Particle size parameter
metrics.meaning: k*a, with k=2*pi*f/c; conservative small-particle gate is 0.1.

metrics.label: Maximum upward force
metrics.meaning: Ideal maximum radiation force; does not establish stable capture.

metrics.label: Effective weight
metrics.meaning: Weight minus buoyancy in the declared medium.

equations.meaning: a radius (m), k wave number (rad/m), E_ac=p_a^2/(4*rho*c^2) energy density (J/m3), Phi dimensionless contrast; z position (m). Force is newton (N).
rho_p particle and rho medium density (kg/m3); g=9.80665 m/s2 is assumed standard gravity.

defaultCalculation.interpretation: Simulated force support, not antigravity. Momentum is exchanged with the acoustic apparatus.

glossary.Pa: Pascal, pressure equal to one newton per square metre.
glossary.K: Kelvin, the SI unit of temperature; temperature differences of 1K and 1°C have equal size.
glossary.ppm: Parts per million; a relative value multiplied by one million.
glossary.ppb: Parts per billion; a relative value multiplied by one billion.
glossary.RLC: A circuit containing resistance R in ohms, inductance L in henry and capacitance C in farad.
glossary.RMS: Root mean square, a waveform amplitude convention distinct from peak.
glossary.DAC: Digital-to-analog converter, the electronic stage that turns numeric samples into a voltage.
glossary.EEG: Electroencephalography, a measured scalp electrical signal; not simulated here.
glossary.SPL: Sound pressure level, an acoustic measurement requiring calibration.
glossary.GLB: Binary glTF, a 3D scene file format; this file contains illustrative geometry.
glossary.SVG: Scalable Vector Graphics, a vector drawing format.
glossary.OSF: Open Science Framework, the repository hosting the independently retrieved registration.
glossary.TOST: Two one-sided tests, an equivalence-testing method; its margin and uncertainty need a declared plan.
glossary.A: Position or condition A in the named protocol; not an ampere unless explicitly stated.
glossary.B: Position or condition B in the named protocol; not magnetic flux density unless explicitly stated.
glossary.LOC1: The external Sphere location-comparison protocol, with its own registered estimand.

sourceRecords.title: Contact-free magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy with acoustic levitation
sourceRecords.readDepth: Abstract, introduction, Results acoustic levitator paragraph, Discussion, Methods acoustic levitation apparatus read; no supplementary datasets or replication.
sourceRecords.passage: The operating frequency of the transducer was set, through an Arduino Uno board and a module Si5351, at 40 kHz.
sourceRecords.claim: Reports contact-free MR imaging/spectroscopy of 0.5–5 microlitre droplets with a demagnetized 40kHz levitator, including apparatus-specific stability and deformation effects.
sourceRecords.limitations: Small droplets and a specific multi-transducer field; not a hollow copper-sphere force calibration, large-body levitation, human health result or validation of this simplified 1D model.

sourceRecords.title: Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics applied to the acoustic levitation of acoustically large objects
sourceRecords.readDepth: Abstract, introduction, Gor’kov small-object methodology and experimental-setup sections read. XML equations contain inline images; equations from image-only content were not recovered or claimed independently transcribed.
sourceRecords.passage: Gorkov’s theory fails to capture the more complex dynamical behaviour exhibited by acoustically large or deformable objects
sourceRecords.claim: Reports separate synthetic small-object benchmark and experimental larger-object identification, illustrating failure of small-sphere extrapolation.
sourceRecords.limitations: Data-driven, setup-dependent dynamics; not a universal extension of Gor’kov or proof that a large copper shell can be supported by the implemented force law.
